title: Showcase signal flow
subtitle: The Chapman Faculty Electroacoustic Showcase, Salmon Recital Hall, 2026-10-18
about: How each of the nine pieces got from the stage (or the laptop at FOH) to the audience: the X32 with an S32 stage box and an SD8 daisy-chained off it, and a separate 8-channel system for TUNNEL. Built from the crew's debrief the day after, the load-in notes and photos. Every box and line says how sure we are: dashed means not confirmed yet, red means it broke during the show. Tap anything for the details.

statuses.confirmed: Seen in a photo or said plainly in the debrief

statuses.unknown: We don't know yet; see the open questions
statuses.failed: Worked in rehearsal, broke during the show

notes.text: I PUNCH PIANOS: self-contained. His own laptop (Windows) running a Max patch, his own SSL 2+ interface, and a MIDI keyboard as a controller. None of it went into our system.

The punches are plain sine waves sent to two speakers lying on the piano's strings; the patch tries to soften each hit and bring out the sustain, with a lot of gain staging and some work on feedback frequencies.
The Max patch fussed during the concert: red clip lights and distortion inside his rig, before it ever reached ours.
Two small speakers placed face down on the strings of the grand piano, driven by Park's own interface. The strings ring in sympathy.
Visible in the photos, lid open, with the mic stand reaching in.
One condenser mic inside the grand piano picks up the strings vibrating from his speakers. That mic is what the house heard.
Another account in the debrief says the one mic was in front of the speaker. Both describe one mic near the speakers.
Condenser: it needs +48 V, switched on from the X32 for its stage box input.
Mic model and S32 input number: unknown.
Polycrisis: a small MIDI keyboard on top of the grand piano (on towels), played in alternation with the piano.
Its only output is 5-pin MIDI, so a cheap 5-pin-to-USB-C adapter took it into the laptop.
Two small issues in practice: the sustain pedal being released, and note-off messages.
Hidden behind the keyboard, running Kontakt (the sampled piano). It kept running with no added latency while the laptop sat at the lock screen.
Output: the laptop's 3.5 mm headphone jack, adapted straight to XLR, with no DI box. The crew calls it sloppy; the S32 handled it fine.
Electrostatic Whale (3) and Blood Memory (8): the same bass clarinetist, front and center, with one mic on a stand.
The photo shows a side-address condenser on a boom stand.
Which stage box and input it used isn't in the notes (S32 is a guess).
Running Spring: electric guitar through a pedalboard into his own laptop (Ableton) and interface, playing along with a track he made. Mostly self-contained.
He wore an earpiece for the playback, fed from his own computer.
His outputs went into the S32 and on to the X32 and the PA (the debrief's words are garbled here).
The plan was discrete channels, but the inputs planned for him were the ones Park's mic was using in the piece before. Fixed at the last minute.
when a tree falls: a laptop and a small MIDI controller (a KORG nanoKONTROL2 in the photo) into a 2-channel Focusrite interface. Its two 1/4" outputs went into the SD8.
Her laptop also drove the projector over HDMI for the live visuals.
The SD8's outputs had failed in Part I, but its inputs still worked, so this piece was fine.
Betweenness: one mic on the table of flower pots the performer plays between MalletKAT phrases.
Into the SD8.
Betweenness: a MalletKAT KAT Pro whose pads trigger vocal-chop samples on her laptop, plus a motion sensor and a double wind wand. The laptop's Scarlett 18i8 sends a stereo pair.
The stereo output went into the SD8.

devices.name: Behringer S32
devices.sub: stage box · 32 in, 16 out · AES50 A and B

notes.text: The hall's S32, on the AES50 A port of the X32. Remote preamps: gain and +48 V are set from the console.
Its AES50 B port feeds the SD8 (the daisy chain).
Normally the X32 listens to it on inputs 25-32 (AES50 A 25-32), and S32 OUT 1-16 carry X32 Outputs 1-16.
Part of the AES50 Cat5 run is partly unshielded. It may explain some odd noises and faults that took unusually long to troubleshoot this semester.
A second stage box on the other side of the stage, daisy-chained off the S32's AES50 B.
Its outputs stopped working during Part I (Electrostatic Whale). Its inputs kept working for the rest of the show.

Daisy-chained after a 32-input S32, the SD8's inputs arrive at the X32 as AES50 A 33-40, so a block of channels has to be routed to them. Its OUTPUT SELECT switch (1-8, 9-16, 17-24) picks which AES50 outputs reach its 8 XLR outs.
The switch position and the X32 input block used that night: unknown.
The FOH Mac mini with its SSL 2+ (four line outputs) played the electronics for Electrostatic Whale and Blood Memory.
Outputs 1-2 (the track) into X32 AUX IN 1-2. Output 3 or 4 (a mono click) into AUX IN 3 or 4, not a regular channel.
Blood Memory's track is a drone: no click. It ran in Logic, so two DAWs were open on the Mac at once. On a Mac that's fine; on Windows, sharing one audio driver between two programs is trouble.
Integrations (1) was a stereo track through the X32 to the mains, with video. That it played from this Mac is a guess.
The hall's full-size X32 mixed everything except TUNNEL.
AES50 A to the S32. Its AES50 A output routing (as photographed 2026-10-20): 1-8 Output 1-8, 9-16 Output 9-16, 17-24 Output 1-8, 25-32 Output 9-16, 33-40 P16 1-8, 41-48 P16 9-16.
Mid-show, a local XLR output on its rear panel replaced the dead SD8 output (see the performer's feed).
The show's input list (which channel each piece used): not recorded.
TUNNEL: 8-channel fixed media and video from one laptop at FOH, on its own system. The X32 wasn't in its path.
Video: a 100-foot HDMI cable from the laptop to the projector.
macOS speaker setup: Left 1, Right 2, Left Surround 3, Right Surround 4, Center 5, LFE 6, Left Center 7, Right Center 8. Those are software labels, not where each speaker stood.
Focusrite Clarett 8PreX on Thunderbolt. Routing inside it is set in Focusrite Control (the original app: Control 2 doesn't support this interface).
On the Mac, some security settings had to be lowered before its driver would load.
Thunderbolt doesn't hot-plug: if the 8PreX ever loses power, the whole computer has to be rebooted. Keep its power plug labeled and leave it on.
Eight 1/4" line outputs, one per speaker.
The sub has only an RCA input, so its signal went through a small mixer: in on a 1/4"-to-XLR cable, the channel fader and the main level set, and out of the mixer's 2-track RCA output.
Which 8PreX output fed it: unknown.
The system buzzed. A Pyle hum destroyer (a ground-loop isolator) on each line fixed it, at the cost of two extra TRS cables per line.
Moving the gear onto one power source didn't fix the buzz first. The Furman M-8X2 filters and protects but doesn't isolate.
Some signal loss was traced to one of these. Whether that one stayed in for the show: unknown.
Everything but TUNNEL reached the audience through the X32's main L/R and the hall's main speakers.
The hall's mains path: X32 to the mains rack, a Crown amp and the ceiling mains L/R.
Electrostatic Whale has a click. The bass clarinetist heard it (and the track) from a stage output: first through the SD8, then, after the SD8's outputs died, straight from the X32.
Wedge or earpiece, and which mix bus: unknown.
A powered sub in the middle of the STAGEPAS ring. It has an RCA input only (unbalanced: worth suspecting when there's hum).
Four Yamaha STAGEPAS systems (three 400s and one 600) used only as amplifiers and speakers: eight speakers, each pair's left and right playing a different channel.
Into the 1/4" stereo line inputs, set to stereo, not mono: the XLR inputs have no pan knob, so they can't keep left and right apart.
Which speaker stood where (front, sides, rear): unknown.
The projector sat behind the screen (back projection), so its image had to be flipped in the projector's settings to read correctly from the front.
Video for Integrations (1), TUNNEL (6) and when a tree falls (7).

paths.name: 1 Integrations
paths.text: Video on the rear-projection screen and a stereo track straight through the X32 to the mains. Where it played from isn't in the notes; the FOH Mac mini is a guess.

paths.name: 2 Betweenness
paths.text: MalletKAT rig (stereo from a Scarlett 18i8) and one flower-pot mic into the SD8 → AES50 through the S32 → X32 → mains.

paths.name: 3 Electrostatic Whale
paths.text: Bass clarinet mic → stage box → X32; the track from the FOH Mac mini on AUX IN 1-2, the click on AUX IN 3 or 4 → the performer only. The SD8 output to the performer died mid-piece: the cable went straight to an X32 local output instead (red: broke; "the fix").

paths.name: 4 I PUNCH PIANOS
paths.text: Park's own laptop and SSL 2+ → two speakers on the piano strings → the strings ring → a condenser in the piano → S32 → X32 → mains.

paths.name: 5 Running Spring
paths.text: Guitar → pedals → his own laptop and interface (Ableton, earpiece for him) → S32 → X32 → mains. The inputs first planned for him were Park's; fixed at the last minute.

paths.name: 6 TUNNEL
paths.text: Its own system: laptop → Thunderbolt → Clarett 8PreX → 8 line outs → hum destroyers → 4 STAGEPAS (8 speakers); a small mixer → RCA → the sub; 100 ft of HDMI to the projector.

paths.name: 7 when a tree falls
paths.text: Laptop and controller → Scarlett 2i2 → SD8 inputs (still fine after its outputs died) → S32 → X32 → mains. Her laptop's HDMI drove the projector.

paths.name: 8 Blood Memory
paths.text: The same setup as Electrostatic Whale, but the track is a drone: no click. Logic on the same Mac mini, alongside the other DAW.

paths.name: 9 Polycrisis
paths.text: Piano and a MIDI keyboard on top of it → 5-pin to USB-C → laptop running Kontakt → 3.5 mm to XLR (no DI) → S32 → X32 → mains.

lessons.title: A stage box's outputs died mid-show
lessons.text: During Electrostatic Whale the SD8 stopped passing outputs; its inputs kept working all night. The fix took a minute: unplug the performer's cable from the SD8, plug it into a local XLR output on the X32, and route the same mix there. Know which console outputs are free before the show, and have a long XLR ready.

lessons.title: Two pieces, one set of inputs
lessons.text: Running Spring was meant to be on its own channels, but they were the ones I PUNCH PIANOS was using in the piece before. Caught at the last minute. One input list for the whole show, every piece on it, prevents this.

lessons.title: Thunderbolt doesn't hot-plug
lessons.text: If the Clarett 8PreX loses power, the laptop has to be rebooted. It also needed lowered security settings and the original Focusrite Control (not Control 2). Label its power, and don't move power cables near it during the show.

lessons.title: Hum in the speaker ring
lessons.text: Moving everything to one power source didn't stop it; a power conditioner isn't an isolator. Ground-loop isolators (Pyle hum destroyers) on each line did. Watch for one that loses signal, and for the unbalanced RCA into the sub.

lessons.title: 3.5 mm into an XLR, no DI
lessons.text: Polycrisis's laptop went headphone jack → XLR straight into the S32 and was fine. The tidy way is a DI box (or a proper line input): balanced, the right level, and a ground lift if it hums.

lessons.title: Two DAWs on one computer
lessons.text: Blood Memory's Logic ran next to the other piece's DAW on the Mac mini without trouble. On Windows, two programs sharing one audio driver is asking for it.

lessons.title: Max patches fuss
lessons.text: I PUNCH PIANOS clipped inside the performer's own patch during the show. When the distortion is upstream of the console, no fader fixes it: talk to the performer about gain inside their rig.

lessons.title: Suspect the cable run
lessons.text: Several odd faults this semester took unusually long to find. Part of the AES50 Cat5 run is partly unshielded; bad mics are the other suspect.
